subject: maths
text: Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be defined as $f(x)=\dfrac{2x^2-3x+2}{3x^2+x+3}$. Then $f$ is:
solution: $y(3x^2+x+3)=2x^2-3x+2\Rightarrow(3y-2)x^2+(y+3)x+(3y-2)=0$. Real $x$ needs $(y+3)^2-4(3y-2)^2\ge0\Rightarrow \tfrac17\le y\le\tfrac75$, so range $\ne\mathbb R$ (not onto). Also $f(x)=f(1/x)$ (e.g. $f(2)=f(1/2)$), so not one-one.

subject: maths
text: Consider the quadratic equation $(n^2-2n+2)x^2-3x+(n^2-2n+2)^2=0$, $n\in\mathbb R$. Let $\alpha$ be the minimum value of the product of its roots and $\beta$ the maximum value of the sum of its roots. Then the sum of the first six terms of the G.P. whose first term is $\alpha$ and common ratio is $\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}$ is:

subject: maths
text: Let $S=\{z\in\mathbb C: z^2+\sqrt6\,iz-3=0\}$. Then $\sum_{z\in S}z^8$ is equal to:

subject: maths
text: The sum of all possible values of $\theta\in[0,2\pi]$ for which the system of equations $x\cos3\theta-8y-12z=0$, $x\cos2\theta+3y+3z=0$, $x+y+3z=0$ has a non-trivial solution, is equal to:
solution: Determinant $=6\cos3\theta+12\cos2\theta+12=0\Rightarrow\cos3\theta+2\cos2\theta+2=0$. With $c=\cos\theta$: $4c^3+4c^2-3c=0\Rightarrow c=0,\ \tfrac12$ ($-\tfrac32$ rejected). $c=0$: $\pi/2+3\pi/2=2\pi$; $c=1/2$: $\pi/3+5\pi/3=2\pi$. Total $4\pi$.

subject: maths
text: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\3&1&0\\9&3&1\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=[b_{ij}]$, $1\le i,j\le3$. If $B=A^{99}-I$, then the value of $\dfrac{b_{31}-b_{21}}{b_{32}}$ is:

subject: maths
text: The sum $1+\dfrac12(1^2+2^2)+\dfrac13(1^2+2^2+3^2)+\dots$ up to 10 terms is equal to:

subject: maths
text: A building has ground floor and 10 more floors. Nine persons enter a lift at the ground floor. The lift goes up to the $10^{th}$ floor. The number of ways, in which any 4 persons exit at a floor and the remaining 5 persons exit at a different floor, if the lift does not stop at the first and the second floors, is equal to:
solution: Allowed floors $3,\dots,10$: 8 floors. Choose the 4 persons: $\binom94=126$; their floor: 8; the other 5 persons' floor: 7. Total $126\cdot56=7056$.

subject: maths
text: Let the mean and the variance of seven observations $2,4,\alpha,8,\beta,12,14$ ($\alpha<\beta$) be 8 and 16 respectively. Then the quadratic equation whose roots are $3\alpha+2$ and $2\beta+1$ is:
solution: Mean: $\alpha+\beta=16$. Variance: $\sum x^2=7(16+64)=560$, so $\alpha^2+\beta^2=560-424=136$, $\alpha\beta=60$, giving $\alpha=6,\beta=10$. Roots $20,21$: $x^2-41x+420=0$.

subject: maths
text: A bag contains 6 blue and 6 green balls. Pairs of balls are drawn without replacement until the bag is empty. The probability that each drawn pair consists of one blue and one green ball is:
solution: $P=\dfrac{36}{66}\cdot\dfrac{25}{45}\cdot\dfrac{16}{28}\cdot\dfrac{9}{15}\cdot\dfrac46\cdot1=\dfrac{16}{231}$.

subject: maths
text: Let $C$ be a circle having centre in the first quadrant and touching the $x$-axis at a distance of 3 units from the origin. If the circle $C$ has an intercept of length $6\sqrt3$ on the $y$-axis, then the length of the chord of the circle $C$ on the line $x-y=3$ is:
solution: Centre $(3,r)$; $y$-intercept $2\sqrt{r^2-9}=6\sqrt3\Rightarrow r=6$. Distance of $(3,6)$ from $x-y=3$ is $6/\sqrt2=3\sqrt2$. Chord $=2\sqrt{36-18}=6\sqrt2$.

subject: maths
text: The eccentricity of an ellipse $E$ with centre at the origin $O$ is $\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$ and its directrices are $x=\pm\dfrac{4\sqrt6}{3}$. Let $H:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ be a hyperbola whose eccentricity is equal to the length of the semi-major axis of $E$, and whose length of latus rectum is equal to the length of the minor axis of $E$. Then the distance between the foci of $H$ is:
solution: Ellipse: $a/e=4\sqrt6/3\Rightarrow a=2\sqrt2$, $b^2=a^2(1-e^2)=2$, minor axis $=2\sqrt2$. Hyperbola: $e_H=2\sqrt2$, $e_H^2=1+b_H^2/a_H^2=8\Rightarrow b_H^2=7a_H^2$; LR $=2b_H^2/a_H=2\sqrt2\Rightarrow 14a_H=2\sqrt2\Rightarrow a_H=\sqrt2/7$. Foci distance $=2a_He_H=2\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt2}{7}\cdot2\sqrt2=\dfrac87$.

subject: maths
text: Let $x=9$ be a directrix of an ellipse $E$, whose centre is at the origin and eccentricity is $\dfrac13$. Let $P(\alpha,0)$, $\alpha>0$, be a focus of $E$ and $AB$ be a chord passing through $P$. Then the locus of the mid point of $AB$ is:
solution: $a/e=9\Rightarrow a=3$, $c=1$, $b^2=8$: $\dfrac{x^2}9+\dfrac{y^2}8=1$, $P=(1,0)$. Chord with midpoint $(h,k)$: $\dfrac{hx}9+\dfrac{ky}8=\dfrac{h^2}9+\dfrac{k^2}8$ passes through $(1,0)$: $8h=8h^2+9k^2$. Locus: $9y^2=8x(1-x)$.

subject: maths
text: If $\sin\left(\tan^{-1}(x\sqrt2)\right)=\cot\left(\sin^{-1}\sqrt{1-x^2}\right)$, $x\in(0,1)$, then the value of $x$ is:
solution: LHS $=\dfrac{\sqrt2x}{\sqrt{1+2x^2}}$; RHS $=\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$. So $2(1-x^2)=1+2x^2\Rightarrow x^2=\tfrac14$, $x=\tfrac12$.

subject: maths
text: The shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x-4}{1}=\dfrac{y-3}{2}=\dfrac{z-2}{-3}$ and $\dfrac{x+2}{2}=\dfrac{y-6}{4}=\dfrac{z-5}{-5}$ is:
solution: $d_1\times d_2=(2,-1,0)$, magnitude $\sqrt5$. Vector between points $=(-6,3,3)$; dot $=-15$. Distance $=15/\sqrt5=3\sqrt5$.

subject: maths
text: Let $\vec a=2\hat i+3\hat j+3\hat k$ and $\vec b=6\hat i+3\hat j+3\hat k$. Then the square of the area of the triangle with adjacent sides determined by the vectors $(2\vec a+3\vec b)$ and $(\vec a-\vec b)$ is:
solution: $(2\vec a+3\vec b)\times(\vec a-\vec b)=-5\,\vec a\times\vec b$. $\vec a\times\vec b=(0,12,-12)$, $|\cdot|^2=288$. Triangle area$^2=\tfrac14\cdot25\cdot288=1800$.

subject: maths
text: Let $\lim_{x\to2}\dfrac{(\tan(x-2))(rx^2+(p-2)x-2p)}{(x-2)^2}=5$ for some $r,p\in\mathbb R$. If the set of all possible values of $q$, such that the roots of the equation $rx^2-px+q=0$ lie in $(0,2)$, be the interval $(\alpha,\beta]$, then $4(\alpha+\beta)$ equals:
solution: Numerator quadratic must vanish at 2: $4r+2(p-2)-2p=0\Rightarrow r=1$; then $x^2+(p-2)x-2p=(x-2)(x+p)$ and limit $=2+p=5\Rightarrow p=3$. Roots of $x^2-3x+q=0$ in $(0,2)$: $D\ge0\Rightarrow q\le\tfrac94$; $f(0)>0$; $f(2)=q-2>0$. So $q\in(2,\tfrac94]$ and $4(2+\tfrac94)=17$.

subject: maths
text: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&3&-1\\2&1&\alpha\\0&1&-1\end{bmatrix}$ be a singular matrix. Let $f(x)=\int_0^x(t^2+2t+3)\,dt$, $x\in[1,\alpha]$. If $M$ and $m$ are respectively the maximum and the minimum values of $f$ in $[1,\alpha]$, then $3(M-m)$ is equal to:

subject: maths
text: Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be such that $f(xy)=f(x)f(y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb R$ and $f(0)\ne0$. Let $g:[1,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be a differentiable function such that $x^2g(x)=\int_1^x\left(t^2f(t)-tg(t)\right)dt$. Then $g(2)$ is equal to:
solution: $f(0)=f(0)f(y)\Rightarrow f\equiv1$. Differentiate: $2xg+x^2g'=x^2-xg\Rightarrow g'+\dfrac3xg=1\Rightarrow x^3g=\dfrac{x^4}4+C$. $g(1)=0\Rightarrow C=-\tfrac14$. $g(2)=\dfrac{4-1/4}{8}=\dfrac{15}{32}$.

subject: maths
text: The area of the region $\{(x,y):x^2-8x\le y\le-x\}$ is:
solution: Intersection: $x^2-8x=-x\Rightarrow x=0,7$. Area $=\int_0^7(7x-x^2)dx=\dfrac{343}2-\dfrac{343}3=\dfrac{343}6$.

subject: maths
text: The value of the integral $\int_{-1}^{1}\left(\dfrac{x^3+|x|+1}{x^2+2|x|+1}\right)dx$ is equal to:
solution: $\dfrac{x^3}{x^2+2|x|+1}$ is odd, integral 0. Remaining $2\int_0^1\dfrac{x+1}{(x+1)^2}dx=2\ln2$.

subject: maths
text: Let $R=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb N\times\mathbb N:\log_e(x+y)\le2\}$. Then the minimum number of elements, required to be added in $R$ to make it a transitive relation, is ______.
solution: $x+y\le e^2\approx7.39\Rightarrow x+y\le7$: $1+2+\dots+6=21$ pairs. Since $(a,1),(1,c)\in R$ for $a,c\le6$, transitivity forces all $(a,c)$ with $a,c\in\{1,\dots,6\}$: 36 pairs. Add $36-21=15$.

subject: maths
text: Let the line $x-y=4$ intersect the circle $C:(x-4)^2+(y+3)^2=9$ at the points $Q$ and $R$. If $P(\alpha,\beta)$ is a point on $C$ such that $PQ=PR$, then $(6\alpha+8\beta)^2$ is equal to ______.
solution: $P$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of $QR$, i.e. on the line through the centre $(4,-3)$ normal to the chord: $P=(4,-3)\pm\tfrac{3}{\sqrt2}(1,-1)$. $6\alpha+8\beta=24-24\pm\tfrac{3}{\sqrt2}(6-8)=\mp\tfrac{6}{\sqrt2}$. Square $=18$.

subject: maths
text: Let the image of the point $P(0,-5,0)$ in the line $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac y1=\dfrac{z+1}{-2}$ be the point $R$ and the image of the point $Q\left(0,-\dfrac12,0\right)$ in the line $\dfrac{x-1}{-1}=\dfrac{y+9}{4}=\dfrac{z+1}{1}$ be the point $S$. Then the square of the area of the parallelogram $PQRS$ is ______.
solution: Foot of $P$ on line 1 is $(-1,-1,1)$, so $R=(-2,3,2)$. Foot of $Q$ on line 2 is also $(-1,-1,1)$, so $S=(-2,-\tfrac32,2)$. $\vec{PQ}=(0,\tfrac92,0)$, $\vec{QR}=(-2,\tfrac72,2)$; $\vec{PQ}\times\vec{QR}=(9,0,9)$, square of magnitude $=162$.

subject: maths
text: Let $f(x)=\begin{cases}x^3+8,&x<0\\x^2-4,&x\ge0\end{cases}$ and $g(x)=\begin{cases}(x-8)^{1/3},&x<0\\(x+4)^{1/2},&x\ge0.\end{cases}$ Then the number of points, where the function $g\circ f$ is discontinuous, is ______.
solution: $g\circ f=x$ for $x<-2$; $\sqrt{x^3+12}$ for $-2\le x<0$; $(x^2-12)^{1/3}$ for $0\le x<2$; $x$ for $x\ge2$. At $x=-2$: $-2$ vs $2$; at $x=0$: $\sqrt{12}$ vs $-12^{1/3}$; at $x=2$: $-2$ vs $2$. Three discontinuities.

subject: physics
text: The percentage error in the calculated volume of a sphere, if there is 2% error in its diameter measurement, is ______.
solution: $V\propto d^3$, so $\Delta V/V=3\times2\%=6\%$.

subject: physics
text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: A. Boltzmann constant, B. Stefan's constant, C. Planck's constant, D. Gravitational constant. List-II: I. $[M^{-1}L^3T^{-2}]$, II. $[ML^2T^{-1}]$, III. $[ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}]$, IV. $[ML^0T^{-3}K^{-4}]$. Choose the correct answer.

subject: physics
text: A solid sphere ($A$) of mass $5m$ and a spherical shell ($B$) of mass $m$, both having same radius, are placed on a rough surface. When a force of same magnitude is applied tangentially at the highest points of $A$ and $B$, they start rolling without slipping with an acceleration of $a_A$ and $a_B$, respectively. The ratio of $a_A$ and $a_B$ is ______.
solution: With $I=kMR^2$ and friction $f$: $F-f=Ma$, $(F+f)R=I a/R$, so $a=\dfrac{2F}{M(1+k)}$. Solid sphere: $a_A=\dfrac{2F}{5m\cdot7/5}=\dfrac{2F}{7m}$. Shell: $a_B=\dfrac{2F}{m\cdot5/3}=\dfrac{6F}{5m}$. Ratio $=\dfrac{2/7}{6/5}=\dfrac5{21}$.

subject: physics
text: A body of mass 1 kg moves along a straight line with a velocity $v=2x^2$. The work done by the body during displacement from $x=0$ to $5$ m is ______ J.
solution: By work-energy theorem $W=\tfrac12m v^2$ at $x=5$: $v=50$, $W=\tfrac12\cdot2500=1250$ J.

subject: physics
text: A cylinder with adiabatic walls is closed at both ends and is divided into two compartments by a frictionless adiabatic piston. Ideal gas is filled in both (left and right) the compartments at same $P,V,T$. Heating is started from left side until pressure changes to $\dfrac{27P}{8}$. If initial volume of each compartment was 9 litres then the final volume in right-hand side compartment is ______ litres. (for this ideal gas $C_p/C_v=1.5$)
solution: Right gas is compressed adiabatically to pressure $27P/8$: $PV^\gamma=\text{const}\Rightarrow V_R=9\left(\tfrac{8}{27}\right)^{1/1.5}=9\cdot\tfrac49=4$ L.

subject: physics
text: For an electromagnetic wave propagating through vacuum, $\vec k$, $\vec E$ and $\omega$ represent propagation vector, electric field and angular frequency, respectively. The magnetic field associated with this wave is represented by:
solution: $\vec B=\dfrac{\hat k\times\vec E}{c}=\dfrac{\vec k\times\vec E}{\omega}$ since $|\vec k|=\omega/c$.

subject: physics
text: Two identical bodies A and B of equal masses have initial velocities $\vec v_1=4\hat i$ m/s and $\vec v_2=4\hat j$ m/s respectively. The body A has acceleration $\vec a_1=6\hat i+6\hat j$ m/s$^2$ while the acceleration of the other body B is zero. The centre of mass of the two bodies moves in ______ path.
solution: $\vec v_{cm}=(2,2)$ and $\vec a_{cm}=(3,3)$ are parallel, so the centre of mass moves along a straight line.

subject: physics
text: Figure represents the extension ($\Delta l$) of a wire of length 1 metre, suspended from the ceiling of the room at one end with a load $W$ connected to the other end. If the cross-sectional area of the wire is $10^{-5}\ \mathrm{m^2}$ then the Young's modulus of the wire is ______ N/m$^2$. (Figure: straight line through the origin of $\Delta l$ (in $10^{-4}$ m) versus $W$ (N); the line passes through $(10\text{ N},1)$, $(20,2)$, ..., $(60,6)$, i.e. $\Delta l=1\times10^{-4}$ m per 10 N.)
solution: $Y=\dfrac{WL}{A\Delta l}=\dfrac{10\times1}{10^{-5}\times10^{-4}}=10^{10}$ N/m$^2$.

subject: physics
text: A cylindrical vessel of 40 cm radius is completely filled with water and its capacity is 528 dm$^3$ (dm: decimeter). The vessel is placed on a solid block of exactly same height as vessel. If a small hole is made at 70 cm below the top of water level, then horizontal range of water falling on the ground in the beginning is ______ cm.
solution: Height $h=\dfrac{528000}{\pi(40)^2}=105$ cm (with $\pi=22/7$). Hole is 70 cm below top, so its height above ground $=105+(105-70)=140$ cm. Range $=2\sqrt{70\times140}=140\sqrt2$ cm.

subject: physics
text: If 2 mole of an ideal monoatomic gas at temperature $T$, is mixed with 6 mole of another ideal monoatomic gas at temperature $2T$ then the temperature of the mixture is:
solution: Energy conservation: $2T+6(2T)=8T_f\Rightarrow T_f=\dfrac{14T}{8}=\dfrac74T$.

subject: physics
text: A spring stretches by 2 mm when it is loaded with a mass of 200 g. From equilibrium position the mass is further pulled down by 2 mm and released. The frequency associated with the system and maximum energy in the spring are ______ Hz and ______ J, respectively. (Take $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$)
solution: $k=mg/x=0.2\cdot10/0.002=1000$ N/m. $f=\dfrac1{2\pi}\sqrt{k/m}=\dfrac{\sqrt{5000}}{2\pi}=\dfrac{5\sqrt{50}}{\pi}$ Hz. Maximum extension $=4$ mm: $E=\tfrac12(1000)(4\times10^{-3})^2=8\times10^{-3}$ J.

subject: physics
text: The electric potential as a function of $x,y$ is given by $V=5(x^2-y^2)$ V. The electric field at a point $(2,3)$ m is ______ V/m.
solution: $\vec E=-\nabla V=(-10x)\hat i+(10y)\hat j=-20\hat i+30\hat j$.

subject: physics
chapter: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
text: A current of 30 A each flows in opposite directions in two conducting wires, placed parallel to each other at a distance of 8 cm. The magnetic field at the mid point between the two wires is ______ $\mu$T. ($\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}=10^{-7}$ N/A$^2$)
solution: Fields add at the midpoint: $B=2\cdot\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi d}=2\cdot\dfrac{2\times10^{-7}\times30}{0.04}=3\times10^{-4}$ T $=300\ \mu$T.

subject: physics
text: A square loop of side 2 cm is placed in a time varying magnetic field with magnitude as $B=0.4\sin(300t)$ Tesla. The normal to the plane of loop makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the field. The maximum induced emf produced in the loop is ______ mV.

subject: physics
text: A sphere of capacitance 100 pF is charged to a potential of 100 V. Another identical uncharged metal sphere is brought in contact with the charged sphere, then the change in the total energy stored on these spheres, when they touch is $\alpha\times10^{-7}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is ______. (combined capacitance of spheres is 200 pF)
solution: $U_i=\tfrac12(100\text{ pF})(100)^2=5\times10^{-7}$ J. After sharing: $Q=10^{-8}$ C, $U_f=\dfrac{Q^2}{2(200\text{ pF})}=2.5\times10^{-7}$ J. Change $=2.5\times10^{-7}$ J, $\alpha=5/2$.

subject: physics
text: The energy released if hydrogen atoms are combined to form ${}^4_2\mathrm{He}$ is ______ MeV. (Take binding energies per nucleon of ${}^2_1\mathrm H$ and ${}^4_2\mathrm{He}$ as 1.1 MeV and 7.2 MeV, respectively)

subject: physics
text: Angle of minimum deviation is equal to the half of the angle of prism in an equilateral prism. The refractive index of the prism is ______.
solution: $A=60^\circ$, $\delta_m=30^\circ$: $\mu=\dfrac{\sin\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}}{\sin\frac A2}=\dfrac{\sin45^\circ}{\sin30^\circ}=\sqrt2$.

subject: physics
text: Refer to the logic circuit given below. For two inputs ($A=1,B=1$) and ($A=0,B=1$), output ($Y$) will be ______. (Figure: $A$ passes through a NOT gate giving $\bar A$; $\bar A$ and $B$ feed an OR gate, and $\bar A$ and $B$ also feed an AND gate; the outputs of the OR and AND gates feed a final NOR gate (OR with output bubble) whose output is $Y$.)
solution: $Y=\overline{(\bar A+B)+(\bar AB)}=\overline{\bar A+B}=A\bar B$. For $A=1,B=1$: $Y=0$; for $A=0,B=1$: $Y=0$.

subject: physics
text: The velocity at which 6 kg mass (shown in figure) strikes the ground when it is released from a height of 6 m above the ground is ______ m/s. Assume pulley is massless and string is light and inextensible. (Take $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$) (Figure: Atwood machine; a 6 kg mass hangs on one side 6 m above the ground, a 2 kg mass rests on the ground on the other side.)
solution: $a=\dfrac{(6-2)g}{8}=5\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$; $v=\sqrt{2ah}=\sqrt{60}\approx7.74$ m/s.

subject: physics
text: In a Young double slit experiment, the wavelength of incident light is 6000 Å, the separation between slits $S_1$ and $S_2$ is 5 cm and the distance between slits plane and screen is 50 cm, as shown in the figure below. If the resultant intensity at $P$ is equal to the intensity due to individual slits, the path difference between interfering waves is ______ Å. (Figure: source $S$ on the axis, slits $S_1,S_2$, screen at 50 cm, point $P$ on the screen away from the central point $O'$.)
solution: $I=4I_0\cos^2(\phi/2)=I_0\Rightarrow\cos(\phi/2)=\tfrac12\Rightarrow\phi=\tfrac{2\pi}{3}$, path difference $=\lambda/3=2000$ Å.

subject: physics
text: A block takes $t$ time to slide down a plane inclined at $45^\circ$ to the horizontal. If the surface is made smooth (frictionless), the block takes time $\dfrac t2$ to slide down the plane. The coefficient of friction between the block and the inclined plane is $\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{100}\right)$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
solution: Rough time is twice smooth time, so $a_{rough}=a_{smooth}/4$: $g(\sin\theta-\mu\cos\theta)=\tfrac14g\sin\theta\Rightarrow\mu=\tfrac34$ at $45^\circ$. $\alpha=75$.

subject: physics
chapter: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
text: The de Broglie wavelength for an electron accelerated through the potential difference of $V_1$ volt is $\lambda_1$. When the potential difference is changed to $V_2$ volt, the associated de Broglie wavelength is increased by 50%. If $(V_1/V_2)=(9/\alpha)$, then the value of $\alpha$ is ______.
solution: $\lambda\propto V^{-1/2}$; $\lambda_2=1.5\lambda_1\Rightarrow V_1/V_2=(1.5)^2=\tfrac94$, so $\alpha=4$.

subject: physics
text: A moving coil of galvanometer when shunted with $2\ \Omega$ resistance gives a full scale deflection for a current of 500 mA. When a resistance of $470\ \Omega$ is connected in series it gives a full scale deflection for 10 V potential applied on it. The value of resistance of galvanometer coil is ______ $\Omega$.
solution: Shunt: $I_gG=(0.5-I_g)2\Rightarrow I_g(G+2)=1$. Series: $10=I_g(G+470)$. Dividing: $10=\dfrac{G+470}{G+2}\Rightarrow9G=450\Rightarrow G=50\ \Omega$.

subject: physics
text: Two cells of emfs 1 V and 2 V and internal resistance $2\ \Omega$ and $1\ \Omega$, respectively connected in parallel, gave a current of 1 A through an external resistance. If the polarity of one cell is reversed, then value of current through the external resistance will be $\dfrac\alpha5$ A. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
solution: Equivalent: $E=\dfrac{1/2+2}{1/2+1}=\dfrac53$ V, $r=\tfrac23\ \Omega$; $1=\dfrac{5/3}{R+2/3}\Rightarrow R=1\ \Omega$. After reversing one cell $|E_{eq}|=\dfrac{2-1/2}{3/2}=1$ V, $I=\dfrac{1}{1+2/3}=\dfrac35$ A. $\alpha=3$.

subject: physics
text: A concave mirror of focal length 10 cm forms an image which is double the size of object when the object is placed at two different positions. The distance between the two positions of the object is ______ cm.
solution: Real image ($m=-2$): $u=-\tfrac32f=-15$ cm. Virtual image ($m=+2$): $u=-\tfrac f2=-5$ cm. Distance between positions $=10$ cm.

subject: chemistry
text: Which of the following contain the same number of atoms? (Given: Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ of H, He, O and S are 1, 4, 16 and 32 respectively) A. 2 g of $\mathrm{O_2}$ gas; B. 4 g of $\mathrm{SO_2}$ gas; C. 1400 mL of $\mathrm{O_2}$ at STP; D. 0.05 L of He at STP; E. 0.0625 mol of $\mathrm{H_2}$ gas. Choose the correct answer.
solution: A: $\tfrac2{32}\times2=0.125$ mol atoms. B: $\tfrac4{64}\times3=0.1875$. C: $\tfrac{1.4}{22.4}\times2=0.125$. D: $\tfrac{0.05}{22.4}\approx0.0022$ (monoatomic). E: $0.0625\times2=0.125$. A, C, E equal.

subject: chemistry
text: The Bohr radius of a hydrogen like species is 70.53 pm. The species and the stationary state ($n$) are respectively (Given: Hydrogen atom Bohr radius is 52.9 pm)
solution: $r=52.9\,n^2/Z\Rightarrow n^2/Z=70.53/52.9=4/3\Rightarrow Z=3,n=2$: $\mathrm{Li^{2+}}$, $n=2$.

subject: chemistry
text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The number of compounds among $\mathrm{SO_2,SO_3,SF_4,SF_6}$ and $\mathrm{H_2S}$ in which sulphur does not obey the Octet rule is 3. Statement II: Among $[\mathrm{H_2O,ClF_3,SF_4}]$, $[\mathrm{NH_3,BrF_5,SF_4}]$, $[\mathrm{BrF_5,ClF_3,XeF_4}]$ and $[\mathrm{XeF_4,ClF_3,H_2O}]$, the number of sets in which all the molecules have one lone pair of electrons on the central atom is 1.
solution: I: $\mathrm{SO_3,SF_4,SF_6}$ violate the octet ($\mathrm{SO_2}$ can satisfy it with a coordinate bond), so 3. II: lone pairs on central atom: $\mathrm{NH_3}$ 1, $\mathrm{BrF_5}$ 1, $\mathrm{SF_4}$ 1 (set 2 only); $\mathrm{H_2O}$ 2, $\mathrm{ClF_3}$ 2, $\mathrm{XeF_4}$ 2. Exactly 1 set. Both true.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

subject: chemistry
text: Match List-I with List-II. Given $V_1$ and $V_2$ are initial and final volumes. List-I (Isothermal process): A. Reversible expansion; B. Free expansion; C. Irreversible compression; D. Cyclic reversible. List-II (Expression): I. $q=0$; II. $q=nRT\ln\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}$; III. $w=-P_{ext}(V_1-V_2)$; IV. $\dfrac{q_{rev}}{T}=0$.
solution: Reversible isothermal expansion of ideal gas: $q=nRT\ln(V_2/V_1)$. Free expansion: $q=0$. Irreversible compression: work given by $P_{ext}\Delta V$ expression (III). Cyclic reversible: $\oint dq_{rev}/T=0$ (state function).

subject: chemistry
text: Given below are two statements (Figure: two chambers separated by a semi-permeable membrane; Chamber 1 has 18 g glucose in 100 mL aqueous solution, Chamber 2 has 30 g glucose in 250 mL aqueous solution). Statement I: $\mathrm{H_2O}$ molecules move from the chamber 1 to chamber 2. Statement II: The osmotic pressure of a solution prepared by dissolving 50 mg of potassium sulphate (molar mass = 174 g/mol) in 2 L of water (at 27 $^\circ$C) is 0.0107 bar. (Given: $R=0.083\ \mathrm{dm^3\,bar\,K^{-1}mol^{-1}}$ and assume complete dissociation of electrolyte)
solution: Chamber 1: 0.1 mol in 0.1 L $=1$ M; chamber 2: $\tfrac{30}{180}/0.25=0.667$ M. Water moves from the dilute (chamber 2) to the concentrated (chamber 1): I false. II: $C=\tfrac{0.05/174}{2}\times3=4.31\times10^{-4}$ M; $\pi=CRT=4.31\times10^{-4}\times0.083\times300=0.0107$ bar: true.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

subject: chemistry
text: Given is a concentrated solution of a weak electrolyte $\mathrm{A_xB_y}$ of concentration '$c$' and dissociation constant '$K$'. The degree of dissociation is given by:
solution: $K=\dfrac{(xc\alpha)^x(yc\alpha)^y}{c(1-\alpha)}\approx c^{x+y-1}x^xy^y\alpha^{x+y}$ (weak, $1-\alpha\approx1$), so $\alpha=\left(\dfrac{K}{c^{x+y-1}x^xy^y}\right)^{1/(x+y)}$.

subject: chemistry
text: For a general redox reaction, Anode: $\mathrm{Red_1\to Ox_1^{n_1+}+n_1e^-}$; Cathode: $\mathrm{Ox_2+n_2e^-\to Red_2^{n_2-}}$. Which of the following statement is incorrect?
solution: Reversible electrical work is the product (charge $\times$ potential difference), $nFE$, not their ratio. The other statements are correct ($E-E^\circ=-\tfrac{2.303RT}{nF}\log Q$).
options: The overall reaction can be written as $n_2\mathrm{Red_1}+n_1\mathrm{Ox_2}\rightleftharpoons n_2\mathrm{Ox_1^{n_1+}}+n_1\mathrm{Red_2^{n_2-}}$
The electrons do not appear in the overall reaction because electrons produced at the anode are consumed at the cathode.
Graph of $\dfrac{(E-E^\circ)F}{RT}$ versus $\log_{10}Q$ (lines for $n=1,2,3$ meeting at $\log Q=0$): slope $\propto\dfrac1n$ (here $n$ is the number of electrons transferred).
If the reaction is carried out reversibly, the electrical work done is equal to the ratio of charge and potential difference through which charge is moved.

subject: chemistry
text: In a period, the first ionisation enthalpy of the element at extreme left and the negative electron gain enthalpy of the extreme right element, except noble gases, are respectively.
solution: Alkali metals have the lowest $\Delta_iH_1$; halogens have the highest (most negative) electron gain enthalpy magnitude.

subject: chemistry
text: Statement I: $\mathrm{F_2O<H_2O<Cl_2O}$ is the correct trend in terms of bond angle. Statement II: $\mathrm{SiF_4}$, $\mathrm{SnF_4}$ and $\mathrm{PbF_4}$ are ionic in nature.
solution: Bond angles: $\mathrm{F_2O}\ 103^\circ<\mathrm{H_2O}\ 104.5^\circ<\mathrm{Cl_2O}\ 110.8^\circ$: I true. $\mathrm{SiF_4}$ is covalent, so II is false.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

subject: chemistry
text: The correct order of first ($\Delta_iH_1$) and second ($\Delta_iH_2$) ionisation enthalpy values of Cr and Mn are: A. $\Delta_iH_1$: Cr > Mn; B. $\Delta_iH_2$: Cr > Mn; C. $\Delta_iH_1$: Mn > Cr; D. $\Delta_iH_2$: Mn > Cr.
solution: $\Delta_iH_1$: Mn (717) > Cr (653). $\Delta_iH_2$: Cr (1591, from stable $3d^5$) > Mn (1509). So B and C.

subject: chemistry
text: Which of the following sequences of hybridisation, geometry and magnetic nature are correct for the given coordination compounds? A. $[\mathrm{NiCl_4}]^{2-}$ - $sp^3$, tetrahedral, paramagnetic; B. $[\mathrm{Ni(NH_3)_6}]^{2+}$ - $sp^3d^2$, octahedral, paramagnetic; C. $[\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}]$ - $sp^3$, tetrahedral, paramagnetic; D. $[\mathrm{Ni(CN)_4}]^{2-}$ - $dsp^2$, square planar, diamagnetic.
solution: A: Ni$^{2+}$ $d^8$ with weak Cl$^-$: $sp^3$, tetrahedral, 2 unpaired e$^-$: correct. B: $sp^3d^2$ octahedral, paramagnetic: correct. C: Ni(0) $d^{10}$, $sp^3$ but diamagnetic: incorrect. D: strong-field CN$^-$: $dsp^2$, square planar, diamagnetic: correct.

subject: chemistry
text: Statement I: A mixture of $\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}$ (sugar) and NaCl can be separated by dissolving sugar in alcohol, due to differential solubility. Statement II: Rose essence from rose petals is separated by steam distillation due to its high volatility and insolubility in $\mathrm{H_2O}$.
solution: Sugar dissolves (sparingly but usefully) in hot alcohol whereas NaCl does not, so the mixture can be separated by differential solubility. Essential oils like rose essence are steam-volatile and immiscible with water. Both statements taken as true.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

subject: chemistry
text: Shown below is the structure of methyl acetate with three different $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ carbon-oxygen bonds: $\mathrm{H_3C-C(=O)_{\alpha}-O-CH_3}$ where $\alpha$ is the $\mathrm{C=O}$ bond, $\beta$ is the $\mathrm{C-O}$ bond of the acyl carbon with the ester oxygen, and $\gamma$ is the $\mathrm{O-CH_3}$ bond. The correct order of bond lengths of these bonds is:
solution: $\mathrm C=\mathrm O$ is shortest. The acyl C-O ($\beta$) has partial double-bond character through resonance with the oxygen lone pair, so it is shorter than the pure single O-CH$_3$ bond ($\gamma$).

subject: chemistry
text: '$x$' is the product which is obtained by the hydrolysis of prop-1-yne in the presence of mercuric sulphate under dilute acidic medium at 333 K. '$y$' is the product which is obtained by the reaction of ethane nitrile with methyl magnesium bromide in dry ether followed by hydrolysis. IUPAC name of product obtained from '$x$' and '$y$' in the presence of barium hydroxide followed by heating is:
solution: Both $x$ and $y$ are acetone. Ba(OH)$_2$ aldol condensation of two acetone molecules, then heating (dehydration), gives mesityl oxide $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm C{=}\mathrm{CH{-}CO{-}CH_3}$: 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one.

subject: chemistry
text: An optically active alkyl bromide $\mathrm{C_4H_9Br}$, reacts with ethanolic KOH to form major compound [A] which reacts with bromine to give compound [B]. Compound [B] reacts with ethanolic KOH and sodamide to give compound [C]. One molecule of water adds to compound [C] on warming with mercuric sulphate and dilute sulphuric acid at 333 K to form compound [D]. The functional group in compound D will be confirmed by:
solution: 2-Bromobutane (chiral) $\to$ but-2-ene [A] $\to$ 2,3-dibromobutane [B] $\to$ but-2-yne [C] $\to$ butan-2-one [D], a methyl ketone, identified by the haloform (iodoform) test.

subject: chemistry
text: Consider the reaction: an ether in which a phenyl ring is bonded to oxygen and the oxygen is attached to a $\mathrm{CH_2}$ attached to a second (saturated) six-membered ring, $\mathrm{Ph{-}O{-}CH_2{-}}$(ring), $+$ HI $\to$ Product. Statement I: In the above reaction, product formed will be a mixture of benzyl alcohol and iodobenzene. Statement II: In the above reaction, the $\mathrm{-O-CH_2-}$ bond is cleaved to give the product.
solution: With HI, aryl alkyl ethers cleave at the O-alkyl bond giving phenol and the alkyl iodide (the aryl C-O bond is not cleaved), so iodobenzene is not formed: I false, II true.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

subject: chemistry
text: Consider the following organic reaction sequence. Choose the final product (X) (consider the major product in all intermediate reactions). Starting material: propanoic acid, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH}$ (drawn in skeletal form). Steps: (i) $\mathrm{NH_3}/\Delta$; (ii) NaOH/$\mathrm{Br_2}$; (iii) $\mathrm{HNO_2/H_2O}$, 0 $^\circ$C; (iv) $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2Cl}$, 0 $^\circ$C.
solution: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH}\to\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CONH_2}\to\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2}$ (Hofmann) $\to\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH}$ (HNO$_2$). Ethanol reduces benzenediazonium chloride to benzene (with acetaldehyde).

subject: chemistry
text: The number of compounds from the following which can undergo reaction with $\mathrm{Br_2}$/KOH (alcoholic) to give respective products and these respective products can also be obtained separately by Gabriel phthalimide reaction is: $\mathrm{C_6H_5CONH_2}$; $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2CONH_2}$; $\mathrm{CH_3CONH_2}$; $\mathrm{C_6H_{11}CONHCH_2CH_3}$; $(\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{C{-}CONHCH_3}$; $\mathrm{C_6H_{11}CONH_2}$ (where $\mathrm{C_6H_{11}}$ is cyclohexyl).
solution: Hofmann bromamide needs a primary amide. $\mathrm{PhCONH_2}\to$ aniline (not by Gabriel). $\mathrm{PhCH_2CONH_2}\to\mathrm{PhCH_2NH_2}$ (Gabriel possible), $\mathrm{CH_3CONH_2}\to\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$ (possible), $\mathrm{C_6H_{11}CONH_2}\to$ cyclohexylamine (taken as obtainable). N-substituted amides fail. Count $=3$.

subject: chemistry
text: Consider the following reactions. Total number of electrons in the $\pi$ bonds and lone pair of electrons in the product (X) is: Glucose ($\mathrm{CHO(CHOH)_4CH_2OH}$) (i) HI, $\Delta$; (ii) $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$/10-20 atm/773 K; (iii) benzoyl chloride/anhyd. $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ $\to$ (X) major product.
solution: Glucose $\to$ $n$-hexane (HI) $\to$ benzene (aromatisation) $\to$ benzophenone $\mathrm{Ph_2C{=}O}$. $\pi$ electrons: $2\times6+2=14$; lone pair electrons on O: $2\times2=4$. Total $=18$.

subject: chemistry
text: Treatment of a gas 'X' with a freshly prepared ferrous sulphate solution gives a compound 'Y' as a brown ring. The compounds X and Y are.
solution: Brown ring test: NO combines with $\mathrm{FeSO_4}$ to form the brown complex $[\mathrm{Fe(H_2O)_5NO}]\mathrm{SO_4}$ (written here as $[\mathrm{Fe(NO)}]\mathrm{SO_4}$).

subject: chemistry
text: An excess of $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ is added to 100 mL of a 0.05 M solution of tetraaquadichloridochromium(III) chloride. The number of moles of AgCl precipitated will be ______ $\times10^{-3}$. (Nearest integer)
solution: $[\mathrm{Cr(H_2O)_4Cl_2}]\mathrm{Cl}$ has only one ionisable $\mathrm{Cl^-}$. Moles of complex $=0.1\times0.05=5\times10^{-3}$, so AgCl $=5\times10^{-3}$ mol.

subject: chemistry
text: An alkane (Y) requires 8 moles of oxygen for complete combustion and on chlorination with $\mathrm{Cl_2}/h\nu$, (Y) gives only one monochlorinated product (Z). The total number of primary carbon atoms in (Y) is ______.
solution: $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}$ needs $\tfrac{3n+1}2=8\Rightarrow n=5$. Only neopentane $\mathrm{C(CH_3)_4}$ gives one monochloro product; it has 4 primary carbons.

subject: chemistry
text: 500 mL of 0.2 M $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ solution in basic medium when mixed with 500 mL of 1.5 M KI solution, oxidises iodide ions to liberate molecular iodine. This liberated iodine is then titrated with a standard $x$ M thiosulphate solution in presence of starch till the end point. If 300 mL of thiosulphate was consumed, then the value of $x$ is ______.
solution: In basic medium $\mathrm{MnO_4^-\to MnO_2}$ (3 e$^-$): $0.1\times3=0.3$ mol e$^-$ (KI excess, 0.75 mol) gives 0.15 mol $\mathrm{I_2}$. $\mathrm{I_2+2S_2O_3^{2-}}$: 0.3 mol thiosulphate in 0.3 L, so $x=1$ M.

text: In a closed flask at 600 K, one mole of $\mathrm{X_2Y_4(g)}$ attains equilibrium as given below: $\mathrm{X_2Y_4(g)\rightleftharpoons2XY_2(g)}$. At equilibrium, 75% $\mathrm{X_2Y_4(g)}$ was dissociated and the total pressure is 1 atm. The magnitude of $\Delta_rG^\ominus$ (in kJ mol$^{-1}$) at this temperature is ______. (Nearest Integer) (Given: $R=8.3\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$; $\ln10=2.3$, $\log2=0.3$, $\log3=0.48$, $\log5=0.69$, $\log7=0.84$)

subject: chemistry
text: Decomposition of a hydrocarbon follows the equation $k=(5.5\times10^{11}\mathrm{s^{-1}})\,e^{-28000\,\mathrm K/T}$. The activation energy of reaction is ______ kJ mol$^{-1}$. (Nearest Integer) Given: $R=8.3\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}mol^{-1}}$
solution: $E_a/R=28000$ K, so $E_a=28000\times8.3=232400$ J/mol $\approx232$ kJ/mol.
